 Order

This petition is filed under Section 438 Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail for release of the petitioner in the event of his arrest registered in Crime No.70/2020 of Athani Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 272, 273, 328 of I.P.C. and under Sections 54, 57, 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Food Safety and Standards Rules-2011.
2. The facts briefly stated in the petition are that, on the complaint filed by A.S.I., Athani Police Station, criminal case is registered, wherein the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.

The allegations are that on the directions of C.P.I., Athani Circle, the complainant-ASI and other police officials conducted raid in the farmhouse in R.S.No.107/1+2/1(b) at Aralihatti village, where accused No.1 was involved in making adulteration in order to increase the quantity of milk by making use of hazardous materials.
On enquiry, it was learnt that accused No.2 was supplying the said hazardous materials for adulteration.
On registering the complaint, the police officials are making attempts to arrest the petitioner.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner-accused No.2 and the learned HCGP for the respondents-State.
Perused the records available at this stage.

4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that when the police have conducted raid, the petitioner was not found at the spot, it is only on the information said to have been disclosed by accused No.1, the petitioner is falsely implicated as accused No.2.
No cogent material has been seized at the time of raid to show that accused No.2-petitioner has supplied the hazardous materials.
Accused No.1 has been granted regular bail.
In the event of arrest and detention, the petitioner will be put to great hardship.

5. Per contra, the learned HCGP submitted that at the time of raid, the hazardous materials which are used for adulteration have been seized, accused Nos.1 and 2 are involved in the illegal activities,
which affects the health of people consuming the adulterated milk.
In the event of granting bail, the accused is likely to commit similar offences.
Thus, the bail petition deserves to be rejected.
6. As could be seen from the complaint averments when the raid was conducted, accused No.1 alone was found at the spot and some hazardous materials used for adulteration have been seized.
On enquiry by the police officials, accused No.1 has told that accused No.2 is supplying the materials for adulteration.
On that basis, the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2011) 1 SCC 694 in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre V/s State of Maharashtra and others, one of the parameters that can be taken into consideration while dealing with the anticipatory bail is frivolity in prosecution and the element of genuineness.

sentences.text: In the event of there being some doubt as to the genuineness of the prosecution, in the normal course of events, the accused is entitled to an order of bail.

While considering the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail, a balance has to be struck between two factors namely, no prejudice should be caused to the free, fair and full investigation and there should be prevention of harassment, humiliation and unjustified detention of the accused.
Generally, arrest should be the last option and it should be restricted to those exceptional cases where arrest of the accused is imperative in the facts and circumstances of the case.
8. The case registered against the petitioner and submission of the learned counsel goes to prove the apprehension of the petitioner regarding his arrest and detention.
The main objection of the prosecution is that in the event of granting bail, the petitioner is likely to supply hazardous materials for adulteration.
The said objection can be set right by imposing stringent conditions.
9. Considering the relevant factors, this Court is of the view that there are valid grounds for granting bail to the accused-petitioner, subject to certain terms and conditions.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer of the concerned police station within fifteen days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order on any working day and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall interrogate the petitioner and enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:
i.
The petitioner shall furnish a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
ii. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer and the Court as and when required.
iii. The petitioner shall co-operate in the investigation.
iv. The petitioner shall not threaten or allure any of the prosecution witnesses.
v. The petitioner shall give attendance to the concerned police station every week on Sunday till conclusion of the trial.
Violation of the above conditions would result in cancellation of the bail automatically.
